# Effect: bitcrusher

Bitcrusher: coarse, dirty digital distortion (8-bit, old samplers, lo-fi texture).

**Where to put it**: Good for drums, lead and a whole lo-fi bus; bits 8-12 is an old sampler, 4-6 is very dirty. Put it before the reverb.

Latest parameters: `muser effects bitcrusher` (MCP: `describe_effect`)

## Parameters

| Parameter | Default | Range | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `bits` | 8 | 1 – 24 bit | Bit depth. 12 slightly grainy; 8 old game console; below 4 very dirty |
| `downsample` | 1 | 1 – 64 × | Downsample factor (hold every Nth sample). 1 = none; 4-8 gives an obvious metallic, jagged sound |
| `mix` | 1 | 0 – 1 | Dry/wet mix. 0.3-0.5 adds just a little grain |

All parameters can be omitted and take their default when omitted; when a value is out of range, `muser validate` reports the exact location.

## Minimal example

```json
{ "type": "bitcrusher", "bits": 10, "downsample": 2, "mix": 0.6 }
```

## Scenario presets

- Grain of an old sampler (lo-fi drums, keys)

  ```json
  {"type": "bitcrusher", "bits": 12, "downsample": 2, "mix": 0.5}
  ```

- 8-bit game console

  ```json
  {"type": "bitcrusher", "bits": 8, "downsample": 4, "mix": 1.0}
  ```

- Very dirty breakup (effect section)

  ```json
  {"type": "bitcrusher", "bits": 4, "downsample": 8, "mix": 0.7}
  ```

## Tips and common mistakes

- Reducing bits raises the noise floor and the high-frequency aliasing; with it on for the whole piece, mix 0.3-0.5 is easier to listen to; fully on suits short sections and fills.
- Put it before the reverb: get dirty first, then enter the space; after the reverb it shatters the tail as well.
- Used together with `tape` it is a common lo-fi chain: tape -> bitcrusher (light) -> eq lowpass.
